utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour. Microphone for the Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon. This is case number IT-02-60/1-A, the Prosecutor versus Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Nikolic, can you hear the proceedings in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, I can follow the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May I have the appearances, please, and we'll start with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Appearing for the Prosecution is Norman Farrell, Ms. Marie-Ursula Kind, and Ms. Susan Grogan. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Virginia Lindsay on behalf of Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. With respect to the subject of the Status Conference, pursuant to Rule 65 bis (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, a Status Conference shall be convened within 120 days after the appeal has been filed. And then 120 days to give the person in custody to file a plea and stating any other matters of business he has. In this particular case, this is the second Status Conference we're holding, and this Status Conference has as its object to allow the appellant to raise any preoccupations he has with respect to the conditions of detention or his state of health, including the mental and physical condition of that person. Mr. Nikolic or his counsel, would you like to tell us anything in that regard which comes under Rule 65 bis (B)?

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I don't believe we have any representations to make in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now with respect to moving forward in the appeals case: As you know, during the last Status Conference, we informed the appellant, and it is the duty of informing the appellant how things stand in the appeals case, and in that sense, the Trial Chamber recognised that the accused, on the 24th of May, 2004, filed an appeal, an appellant's brief, and the Prosecutor responded on the 5th of July, 2004. Now, as far as those two filings are concerned and those two briefs, I have asked that any confidential elements be redacted from the brief so that we can have public versions of the appellant brief. Mr. Nikolic, I should also like to inform you on this occasion, actually to remind you that in keeping with our decision of the 15th of July, 2004, your response must be filed by the 5th of August, 2004. So that is the deadline for you to respond to the response made to your appellant brief. So that, then, is the deadline which you have to meet. The Chamber would also like to say that it has to see to another matter, an appeal lodged by the Prosecution for certain things to be deleted from the appellant's brief, and that was filed on the 5th of June, 2004. It seems that Mr. Nikolic has agreed to having those matters deleted and redacted from the brief, in -- but he insists on keeping paragraphs 122 and 174, as well as paragraph 227 in part. I should like to inform the parties that the request made by the Defence to extend the deadline and to enable the filing of a response refers to the two briefs, the first on the 28th of June, 2004, and all this will be dealt with when the first brief is considered. The Appeals Chamber has also received a request by the Defence. It is a request seeking additional evidence, and the date that was filed was the 18th of June, 2004. And then on the 21st of June, 2004, we received an additional brief in that regard. So in fact, the Appeals Chamber has received all the briefs and the Chamber will rule on the proposals and requests made in its full composition. Now, as to any further matters, I have nothing more to put forward at this present Status Conference, so I'm just going to ask the parties whether they wish to take the floor, whether anybody wishes to make any remarks or make any comments. Shall we start with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it would be better if we started with the Prosecution. I think they have representations to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Farrell, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just to update you on some dealings between the Defence counsel and the Prosecution, if I may, Your Honour. First of all, Ms. Lindsay has indicated that she takes issue with some of the representations in the Prosecution's response brief, and I've met with her, and I'm more than willing to review the aspects of the Prosecution's response brief that she takes issue with, and if there's any mistakes or changes that have been made in the Prosecution's response brief, the Prosecution, of course, will undertake to file a core agendum corrigendum. Ms. Lindsay was quite fair. Instead of filing a motion she brought to my attention some issues that she disputed in the Prosecution's response, so I'm in the midst of looking at those and if there are some things that can be corrected in the Prosecution's response brief, as indicated, after looking at her representations, the Prosecution can file a corrigendum. There's some dispute as to the wording of the original plea agreement and the representations about the plea agreement. I think the result, then, is that Ms. Lindsay has indicated to me that if the Prosecution was to make some corrections to its response brief, that she would then be in a position to file her reply brief but that she may need some additional time, depending on what the Prosecution can agree to, if the Prosecution changes some of the content of the response brief. The bottom line, quite simply, is that the appellant has alleged that some of the representations in the Prosecution's response brief are not completely consistent with the plea agreement. So with the Court's indulgence, of course, I intend to review the Prosecution's response brief and ensure that it's consistent with the plea agreement at trial, and will inform Ms. Lindsay and will, of course, as I said, file a corrigendum. I think Ms. Lindsay may indicate that she may need more time if the Prosecution's position is in any way altered or changed by any corrections we have to make to our brief, and I've indicated to Ms. Lindsay if there's any delay that's at the far -- as a result of the fault of the Prosecution, that I wouldn't oppose a short period of time for her to properly respond. I think that generally covers the discussions that have taken place between Ms. Lindsay and myself. At this stage, I don't think there's anything for the Court to do except for it to be informed that the Prosecution may file a corrigendum to some of the submissions it made in its response brief, and simply to inform you as well, Your Honour, that that may affect the time period that Ms. Lindsay may need to file her reply. But I think that's a matter that will take a few days for me to look at the response brief. Thank you for your indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Farrell. Thank you for the explanations you have just provided us with. You have the floor, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There's a couple of matters I'd like to address. The first one is the corrections that are needed in the Prosecution's response brief. I'd just like the Court to be aware that we met on the 16th of April [sic] to discuss the issue of factual inaccuracies in the response brief, and we met with both Mr. Farrell and Mr. McCloskey, and at that meeting, Mr. McCloskey confirmed that there are in fact factual errors in the response brief. Since 16th of July, we've tried to work with the Prosecution in order to resolve these issues, but for whatever reasons it's -- the Prosecution has not been able to move very quickly on this matter. So I would just like the Appeals Chamber to be aware that there is a slight possibility and we're doing everything we can to avoid it. It's not what we want to happen. But there is a possibility that we will be filing a motion to vary our grounds of appeal if we're unable to resolve the matter. The other matter that I want to address is that a mistake that was made by the Trial Prosecutor, Mr. McCloskey. Prior to Mr. Nikolic's guilty plea, Mr. McCloskey knew that one of the named victims in the indictment did not die in the circumstances that are set forth in the indictment. And Mr. Farrell has agreed that this was a mistake and that the indictment needs to be corrected and we're working together to try to resolve that issue without resort to Rule 115 proceedings. But again, there is a slight possibility that there will be an additional motion to admit additional evidence. I'm asking for ten days from when a correction is filed within which to file Mr. Nikolic's reply brief. The factual errors in the Prosecution's response brief arise from the factual basis of the guilty plea, and as such, they impact directly upon the legal arguments in ground III which deals with Mr. Nikolic's role in the crime and ground V(D)(3) which involves the timing of the guilty plea. Until I can be certain of the corrections made by the Prosecution, I am unable to advise Mr. Nikolic as to what course his appeal should take. And I'm unable to draft his reply brief in relation to two very important sections of the reply brief. And so for those reasons I would respectfully request that the Prosecution be asked to state or this Court set a date certain by which the Prosecution must respond to our request for corrections, and that I then have ten days from the filing of any corrections within which to file the reply brief. So those are my only representations, Your Honour, unless you have any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Farrell, would you like to indicate when you will be ready to file a reply which will be corrected. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you. It's my hope that we'll be able to do it by the end of the week. I'll make that representation to you, Your Honour. The difficulty is, to be frank, I have five Status Conferences this week, the Blaskic Appeals Chamber decision coming out, the filing in the Simic brief tomorrow, and a filing in another brief on Thursday. So all I can say is I'll do my best to get something by the end of this week, or I'll indicate to the Court if I'm unable to. And while I'm on my feet, I'd just like to note two matters. One, I don't -- it might have just been a mistake, but one of the notations in the record said that the Prosecution met with Ms. Lindsay on the 16th of April. I think that might have been just -- I think it was July -- subsequently she said the 16th of July and I think it was only just over a week ago Friday that we met to discuss this on July 16th. And secondly, she had indicated that regarding one of the victims in the indictment, that I had agreed that there was a mistake. I had agreed that if this was the case, it would certainly be an issue that I think would be problematic. I'd prefer to reserve my opinion on whether there was any errors until I've had a chance to review the record, if you don't mind. Thank you. If that's satisfactory to Your Honour, Judge Guney, I'll give you either something by Friday, or certainly an indication if I'm unable to make that deadline with the deadline when I can file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Farrell. The Prosecutor has indicated to us that he will be ready to file a corrected representation not later than the end of this week. You have the floor, Ms. Lindsay.

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If they do that, then if I could have until the 10th of August, is what I would be requesting, an additional five days. That would be ten days from when they file the corrections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can request that, but you have to do it in writing.

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you confirm, Mr. Farrell, what you have -- can you confirm what Mr. Farrell has told us, that the meeting took place in July, on the 16th of July, rather than on the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It was last Friday, the 16th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Are there any issues to raise at this point?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I myself have no issues to raise at this Status Conference, and if there are no other issues to raise, the Status Conference can be adjourned. It is so decided. The Status Conference is adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
